spec_features.spec_quote: The per-condition budgets are knobs partly so this exposure can be kept to the minimum needed for a given analysis.
spec_features.evidence: n_rollouts is read per-condition in conditions.build_rollouts (conditions.py:127 `n_rollouts = int(spec["n_rollouts"])`) and bounds how many conversations are generated; configured per condition in configs/eval.yaml (e.g. impossible_numeric_3turn n_rollouts: 250). run_elicitation.py:36-37 further caps total rollouts: `if args.limit: rollouts = rollouts[: args.limit]`. These values actually drive the elicitation loop length (run_elicitation.py:45 `for i, ro in enumerate(rollouts)`), so exposure volume is genuinely enforced.
spec_features.notes: The knobs are real and enforced, but the code frames them as smoke-test / cost knobs, not exposure-minimization. No distress-aware cap (nothing reads frustration scores to stop early); only a fixed conversation-count budget.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Adjust `n_rollouts` down for cheap smoke tests. ... --limit help='optional cap on total rollouts (smoke test)'

spec_features.spec_quote: The paper itself cautions this may suppress expression without addressing any underlying state; the layer-ablation/probing hook ... is retained
spec_features.evidence: `layers_to_transform` is genuinely wired into training: train_dpo.py:54 and train_sft.py:62 do `layers_to_transform=lc.get("layers_to_transform")` and pass it to LoraConfig, so setting it would restrict LoRA to specific layers. It executes. Default is null (configs/train_dpo.yaml:31, train_sft.yaml:29) so no ablation runs by default, and there is NO probing implementation at all (no probe/readout code exists; only the LoRA layer-restriction half of the 'ablation/probing' hook is built).
spec_features.notes: The claim couples 'layer-ablation' AND 'probing'; only the layer-restriction LoRA config is implemented and wired. No probing code. Also note this is a training-method knob, not a mechanism that bounds/softens/monitors the subject's distress exposure.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: For the layer-ablation experiments in Section 4.2 ("internal vs expressed"), restrict to a layer range

code_only_features.feature_name: reassurance prefix/suffix softening subject during calm-data generation
code_only_features.evidence: calm_data.add_reassurance_to_initial / add_reassurance_to_followup (calm_data.py:37-44) inject a calming Table-4 prefix/suffix into the subject's prompts; these are actually applied in scripts/generate_calm_data.py:40-41 when reassure=True, genuinely softening what the subject is exposed to in that pipeline. (It is later stripped only from the training data, not from the live conversation.)
code_only_features.justification_quote: with reassurance (prefix + suffix) -> tends to produce calm responses ... To build the finetuning data we filter to responses scoring 0 or 1
